files.AUDIT-REQUEST.md:
# Checkout form - audit request


`checkout-form.html` is the checkout page as it currently stands. Support has
three complaints from assistive-technology users:

1. A screen reader user could not tell what the email field was for once they
   had started typing in it.
2. A keyboard-only user could not submit the order.
3. The order-confirmation link "Click here" was reported as meaningless when
   navigating by link.

The team wants the audit written up before the next release. Product has asked
twice whether the page "passes WCAG" - the answer needs to distinguish what
automated tooling can establish from what only a real screen reader test can.

No automated report has been produced yet. `checkout-form.html` is the only
input available.

all.why: maps the grey hint text to the contrast criterion
separates manual checks from what the source shows

any.why: recommends a native button for the div control

expectations: Each finding maps to a WCAG success criterion, and no finding presents a 44x44px touch target as an AA requirement (24x24 CSS px is SC 2.5.8 at AA; 44x44 is SC 2.5.5 at AAA).
The icon-only clear-cart button is reported as having no accessible name, and the #9aa0a6 hint text is reported as failing SC 1.4.3 contrast on the white background.
The div-based 'Place order' control is reported as not keyboard operable, and the fix is a native <button> rather than adding role and tabindex to the div.

The email input is reported as relying on its placeholder with no persistent visible label, and an associated <label> is recommended ahead of an ARIA-only fix; the reply does not claim the page passes WCAG, and screen-reader behavior is marked as needing a manual check with a named browser and screen reader pair.

cases.prompt: axe reports zero violations on our new modal. Can I tell product it is WCAG 2.2 AA compliant and close the ticket?

any.why: raises focus handling, which axe cannot check

none.why: does not open with a plain yes

expectations: States that a clean automated scan is not proof of WCAG conformance and that keyboard and screen-reader behavior need manual testing.
Points out concrete gaps axe would not catch in this modal: focus is not moved into the dialog on open, not kept inside it, and not returned to the trigger on close, and Escape does not close it.
Gives a specific manual test plan or code changes to address those gaps before the ticket is closed.
